reason: The commit renames the cleanup protocol from finish to free without materially changing lifecycle behavior. H0 still creates, opens, reads, closes, and destroys a read archive; its archive_read_finish(a) call remains available under ARCHIVE_VERSION_NUMBER < 4000000 and dispatches through archive_free to the same renamed _archive_read_free implementation. The write-side changes are likewise finish-to-free aliases and internal call-site migrations, not a new input-driven attack surface or state protocol requiring this read harness to expand.
evidence: archive_read_finish in archive_virtual.c now returns (a->vtable->archive_free)(a), exactly as archive_read_free does.
archive_read_vtable assigns av.archive_free = _archive_read_free, so H0's archive_read_finish(a) reaches the changed cleanup implementation.

_archive_read_free retains the prior _archive_read_finish behavior: it checks ARCHIVE_STATE_ANY, calls archive_read_close when needed, cleans formats and strings, frees a->entry, clears magic, and frees a.

H0 exercises both cleanup states: its decompression path calls archive_read_finish after reading, while its fuzz loop may call archive_read_close before archive_read_finish or invoke archive_read_finish after an open failure.
archive_write_free and archive_write_finish both dispatch to archive_free; the production call-site edits replace the legacy synonym without introducing new write semantics.
recommended_action: No harness maintenance is needed for this commit; retain H0.
